title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes build an axiomatic tame geometry. A 'figure' is a finite admissible set of 'variétés' (closed pieces X with open parts or strata X°) in an ambient set E, partially ordered by inclusion and closed under taking faces. This makes it something like a finite stratified space or a regular cell complex. Page 28 defined two figures F and G to be 'ensemblistement compatibles' (compatible as sets) by equivalent conditions. The key one, b', says that for X∈F and Y∈G, either X°∩Y°=∅ or X=Y; equivalently, F∪G is admissible and F, G are saturated in it. F and G are then called 'compatibles' if moreover F∪G is a figure having F and G as sub-figures (it amalgamates as F ⊔_{F∩G} G). A 'configuration' is a set of pairwise compatible figures.

Page 29:
(1) Conjecture 4 is a local-to-global criterion. Let a 'multiplet' X̂ be the sub-figure generated by one variété X, i.e. X together with all its faces (the closure or star of one cell). If every multiplet of F is compatible with every multiplet of G, then F and G are compatible. The converse is evident. A margin note adds that under this hypothesis F and G are already compatible as sets. That is immediate, because condition b' only involves pairs (X,Y), and X ∈ X̂, Y ∈ Ŷ.
(2) Consequence (corollary). A family (F_i) of figures is a configuration iff for all i≠j and all multiplets X̂ of F_i and Ŷ of F_j, X̂ and Ŷ are compatible. If I is finite, then F=∪F_i is a figure and each F_i is a sub-figure of it. So compatibility of arbitrary finite families is reduced to compatibility of pairs of single closed cells.
(3) A struck-out NB begins to discuss the converse aim (an invariant attached to every pair {F,G}).
(4) Definition: a 'contexte' (the axiomatic framework) is called 'ensembliste', or a 'contexte de points', if set-theoretic compatibility already implies compatibility. In such a context Conjecture 4 is trivial.

The next page says that for non-set-theoretic structures this should be reformulated. It introduces the point figures F_x={{x}} and calls distinct points x, y 'disjoint' when {F_x,F_y} is a figure. Compatibility of figures then becomes a genuinely extra structure, not determined by the underlying point sets.

Purpose: to axiomatize when pieces of tame geometry can be glued without refinement, and to isolate the 'pointwise' (set-theoretic) contexts from more general ones.
errors: Conjecture 4 is stated without proof. In a context de points it is trivial, as Grothendieck notes. In general it depends on the unstated axioms for figures; the frontier/admissibility part of compatibility is not obviously local in multiplets.

The finite-union claim (pairwise compatibility implies that ∪F_i is a figure) needs an amalgamation axiom. Pairwise amalgamation does not automatically give n-fold amalgamation without some coherence; the text gives no argument.

ideas.what: Compatibility of two figures (stratified finite complexes) as: union is a figure containing both as sub-figures, i.e. a pushout over the intersection
ideas.modern_name: compatible stratifications / union of subcomplexes in a common regular cell complex; definable cell decompositions compatible with given sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom stratification theory; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame topology only programmatically; this axiomatic detail does not appear there

ideas.what: Conjecture 4: compatibility of figures can be tested on pairs of multiplets (closures of single cells)
ideas.modern_name: local-to-global (cellwise) criterion for gluing stratified sets

ideas.what: Configuration = pairwise compatible family of figures; finite configurations glue to a figure

'Contexte ensembliste' / 'contexte de points': contexts where compatibility is determined by the underlying point sets; versus non-set-theoretic contexts where it is extra structure (next page: 'disjoint points')
ideas.modern_name: roughly: 'spatial' versus 'pointless' frameworks for tame topology; comparable to locales versus spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct analogue in tame-topology literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck envisages axiomatic analysis-situs 'contexts' that are not determined by points. In these, compatibility of figures (and 'disjointness' of points, next page) is additional data. Conjecture 4 is meant to be a nontrivial local-to-global axiom precisely there. He never developed this, and o-minimality, the standard modern framework for tame topology, is entirely point-set based.
missed.quote: Le contexte est dit "ensembliste", ie "contexte de points" ... si deux figures ensemblistement compatibles sont compatibles (ce qui rend donc triviale la Conj 4)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a 'pointless' or relational axiomatization of tame topology, in which gluing data is primitive. That could connect with combinatorial or poset models of stratified spaces and with exit-path or ∞-categorical stratified homotopy theory. It is only a sketch, though.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly routine bookkeeping on gluing stratified 'figures'. The only mildly interesting feature is the explicit separation of 'contextes de points' from non-set-theoretic contexts in an axiomatic tame topology, which is undeveloped and not in the literature, but is a small seed rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: Margin NB reads approximately 'NB Alors F et G sont ens.[emblistement] comp.[atibles]', not 'ens. conv.'.

The heading 'Contre-ex [-ensemblistes-] {+de points+}' should read 'Contextes [-ensemblistes-] {+de points+}'. Likewise 'Le contre-ex est dit "ensembliste", ie "contexte de points"' should read 'Le contexte est dit ...'.
'G^*' — the asterisk appears to be a reference mark rather than a dual or modified G; unsure.
